Editorial diagnostics, not predictions.

A1.why: Adds a how-to for the Nordic (described, no invented dose) and the stretching distinction as a plain statement; longer, so concision is 7.

B1.why: The staircase image now has a 'training' rung; the ending separates 'back to training' from 'back to the match', the exact distinction the brand teaches.

A2.why: Adds the why (ligaments heal + fast-reacting muscles) between the trial and the demo; labelled as a principle.

B2.why: The verified mechanism (heavy slow resistance raised collagen turnover) explains *why* loading beats rest.

B3.why: Says why the number matters (squat and landing compensations, framed as 'may'), before the measurement-error turn.

EP01.why: = S1. The stress-fracture science is now part of the story (what it is, refracture and warning pain), and the ending gives a red flag the viewer can act on.

EP02.why: = S7. The ankle science sits mid-story; the ending links to the balance-training trial.

GEDO.why: Rebuilt around two documented fatigue/substitute numbers (−12% second half; subs +15%). The story now teaches performance physiology.

EP5.why: Kept from v5 (science correction already applied).

S1.learn: What a stress fracture is (repeated load faster than bone repair), that it can recur (a third were refractures in an MT-5 cohort) and often gives warning pain; act early.

S2.learn: Why a hamstring tear takes weeks when pain settles in days (the lengthening load at sprint speed), the 16% re-injury rule of thumb, and that return is set by top-speed tolerance.

S3.learn: Concussion needs no blackout; symptoms can be delayed; suspected = remove, no same-day return, graded return; a happy ending doesn't validate playing on.

S4.learn: What the ACL does, what reconstruction is, why ~9 months matters (−51% per month to 9 months), and that only ~2/3 return to their previous level: time AND criteria.

S5.learn: Why the shoulder dislocates (shallow socket, soft-tissue restraints), the 39% recurrence after a first dislocation, and why goalkeepers' positions shape the rehab.

S6.learn: What the meniscus does, why the inner part heals poorly (no blood supply), and why initial timelines are estimates that the knee's response overrides.

S7.learn: How common ankle injuries happen in general, why walking returns long before duels, and that balance training cut re-sprains 33% → 22%. Integrity 8: Zidan's own diagnosis isn't public.
